coverageRationale.zh: 把 ISO/IEC 11770-2:2018 的 13 个对称密钥建立机制、Point-to-Point/KDC/KTC 三环境、KDF 与密钥确认写成可复述公式；区分 KDC 生成密钥与 KTC 转换密钥。
coverageRationale.en: Rewrites ISO/IEC 11770-2:2018 as reproducible formulas: 13 symmetric key-establishment mechanisms across Point-to-Point, KDC and KTC, with KDF and key confirmation; it distinguishes a KDC that generates keys from a KTC that translates them.

credit.zh: 原创示意图（目录级模型）

zh.principle: **标准**：对称技术密钥管理（Key management — Part 2: Mechanisms using symmetric techniques）。ISO/IEC 11770-2:2018 把对称密钥建立分成三类环境：Point-to-Point 6 个机制、KDC 4 个、KTC 3 个，共 13 个。它只规定消息中必须携带的密钥材料与建立条件，不规定消息格式、错误消息、初始密钥建立、跨域管理或实现兼容性。通用式 K=f(F,I_A,I_B,TVP_A,TVP_B,SID)：F 是 keying material，I 是实体标识，TVP 是随机数/时间戳/序列号，SID 是会话标识；f 是密钥派生函数。机制 1 只用 TVP 派生，机制 2 由 A 选 F 并用既有 K_AB 加密传送，二者不提供实体认证。机制 6 用双方各自持有的 F_A、F_B 与 TVP 经 KDF 生成 K，可附 I_A、I_B、Text、SID，并用随机数做密钥确认。机制 7 由 KDC 生成或取得 F，分别用 A、B 与 KDC 的长钥加密成两条消息，A 转发第二条给 B。机制 12 是 KTC：A 自己选 K_AB，服务器只把它转换成 B 可解的封装，不生成密钥。密钥确认不是实体认证的同义词：它只证明对方持有同一 K；实体认证还要证明对方是声称的实体，通常靠签名或额外协议。
zh.why: Part 2 的公式级价值在于区分“谁选密钥、谁看密钥、谁确认密钥”。Point-to-Point 适合双方已有长钥；KDC 适合中心化分发但中心知道密钥；KTC 适合一方控制密钥、中心只做转换。三者的信任假设不同，不能用一个“密钥分发”标签糊过去。13 个机制不是 13 个算法；它们是消息编排。KDF 的选择、TVP 的 freshness、密钥确认的方向、SID 的绑定，决定协议能否抵抗重放、反射与未知密钥共享。为什么公式里要写 I_A/I_B/SID：不把身份和会话绑进派生输入，跨会话密钥可能相同；不绑 TVP，重放可能通过。
zh.used: 选型顺序：先看双方是否有共享长钥；有则点对点，需中心则 KDC，需一方保留密钥控制权则 KTC。再定 KDF：用 ISO/IEC 11770-6 或成熟 HKDF/KDF，输入身份、随机数、SID 与用途标签。消息中至少绑定协议版本/机制标识、发起方/响应方标识、TVP、密钥用途。密钥确认用 MAC_{K_AB}(TVP_B||I_A||I_B) 之类的绑定，不能只发“OK”。工程检查：长钥是否预置且不重用；TVP 是否唯一；KDC/KTC 是否在信任边界内；密钥确认是否双向；错误消息是否泄露密钥状态；是否把 MAC 钥与加密钥分离。
zh.broken: 标准不建立初始长钥；没有初始信任，任何机制都空转。机制 1/2 无实体认证，易受中间人/重放；KDC 被攻破则所有派生密钥暴露；KTC 可能看到或替换密钥材料。TVP 重用、KDF 输入不足、密钥确认缺失、SID 不绑定、把同一密钥用于加密与 MAC，都会破坏安全。产品符合标准不等于产品互通；消息格式不在标准范围内。它也不处理跨域密钥管理、密钥生命周期、实现侧信道；这些分别看 Part 1、Part 7 与实现标准。
zh.history:
1996 年第一版；2008 年第二版技术修订，修改机制 12 的安全缺陷；2018 年第三版更新 Clause 5 要求、给加密串加可选消息/机制标识、扩展机制 5 的密钥计算输入、微调机制 8 第四条与机制 10 第二条消息；2024 年复审确认。

**技术参数与复算边界**

该条目的形式模型是 \(S=\min_i S_i,\quad S_i\in\{\text{密钥强度},\text{分组安全},\text{实现安全}\}\)。输入：输入：对称技术密钥管理的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：S 为综合安全强度；各分量取最小值，不能只看密钥位数。 预期输出：按 对称技术密钥管理 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。

复杂度由密钥长度、分组/状态规模、轮数、随机数质量和敌手模型共同决定；参数越界、版本差异与实现侧信道都可能使公式结论失效。已登记限制：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。

en.principle: **Standard**: Key management — Part 2: Mechanisms using symmetric techniques (对称技术密钥管理). ISO/IEC 11770-2:2018 divides symmetric key establishment into three environments: six Point-to-Point mechanisms, four KDC mechanisms and three KTC mechanisms, 13 in total. It specifies only the keying material and conditions that messages must carry; message formats, error messages, initial key establishment, inter-domain management and implementation compatibility are outside its scope. The general form is K=f(F,I_A,I_B,TVP_A,TVP_B,SID): F is keying material, I are entity identifiers, TVP is a random number, timestamp or sequence number, SID is a session identifier, and f is a KDF. Mechanism 1 derives from TVP only; mechanism 2 has A choose F and encrypt it under an existing K_AB; neither provides entity authentication. Mechanism 6 derives K from F_A and F_B plus TVPs, optionally with I_A, I_B, Text and SID, and uses random numbers for key confirmation. Mechanism 7 has a KDC generate or acquire F and encrypt two messages under A's and B's long-term keys with the KDC; A forwards the second part to B. Mechanism 12 is a KTC: A chooses K_AB and the server only translates it into a package B can open; the server does not generate the key. Key confirmation is not a synonym for entity authentication: it proves possession of the same K, while entity authentication also proves that the peer is the claimed entity, usually through a signature or an additional protocol.
en.why:
The formula-level value of Part 2 is separating “who chooses the key, who sees it, and who confirms it”. Point-to-Point suits parties that already share a long-term key; a KDC suits central distribution but the centre knows the key; a KTC suits a case where one party controls the key and the centre only translates it. Their trust assumptions differ and cannot be hidden under one “key distribution” label.

The 13 mechanisms are not 13 algorithms; they are message choreographies. KDF choice, TVP freshness, direction of key confirmation and SID binding determine whether the protocol resists replay, reflection and unknown-key sharing.

That is why the formula includes I_A, I_B and SID: without identity and session binding, keys can repeat across sessions; without TVP binding, replay can pass.
en.used:
Selection order: first ask whether the parties already share a long-term key. If yes, use Point-to-Point; if a centre is required, use KDC; if one party must keep control of the key, use KTC. Then choose a KDF: ISO/IEC 11770-6 or a mature HKDF/KDF, with identities, random numbers, SID and purpose labels as input.

Messages should bind at least protocol version or mechanism identifier, initiator and responder identities, TVP and key purpose. Key confirmation should use a binding such as MAC_{K_AB}(TVP_B||I_A||I_B), not a bare “OK”.

Engineering checks: is the long-term key pre-shared and non-reused; is each TVP unique; are KDC/KTC inside the trust boundary; is confirmation mutual; do error messages leak key state; are MAC and encryption keys separated.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken:
The standard does not establish an initial long-term key; without initial trust every mechanism stalls. Mechanisms 1 and 2 have no entity authentication and are exposed to man-in-the-middle and replay; a compromised KDC exposes all derived keys; a KTC may see or replace keying material.

TVP reuse, insufficient KDF input, missing key confirmation, unbound SID, or using one key for both encryption and MAC all break security. Product compliance is not product interoperability; message formats are out of scope.

It also does not handle cross-domain key management, key life cycle or implementation side channels; see Part 1, Part 7 and implementation standards.
en.history: The first edition appeared in 1996; the second edition in 2008 was a technical revision that changed mechanism 12 to address a security shortcoming; the third edition in 2018 updated Clause 5 requirements, added an optional message/mechanism identifier to encrypted strings, expanded the key-calculation inputs of mechanism 5, made minor changes to the fourth message of mechanism 8 and the second message of mechanism 10, and was confirmed in 2024.
